原标题: Azerbaijan to raise renewables share to 34% by end-2027
原文节选:
QAZAQ GREEN. Azerbaijan plans to increase the share of renewable energy sources (RES) in its total installed power generation capacity to 34% by the end of 2027, Deputy Energy Minister Elnur Soltanov said during a panel discussion at the Baku Climate Action Week 2026 (BCAW 2026), according to Report .az.

The share of renewables currently stands at 21%. According to Soltanov, renewable energy generation in Azerbaijan is expected to nearly double this year compared with 2025.

“Azerbaijan already operates the largest solar and wind power plants in the region. Despite its relatively small territory and economy, the country seeks to become a regional leader in the green transition,” he said.

原标题: QazaqGreen
原文节选:
QAZAQ GREEN. Deep porous rock formations could be used to store renewable electricity for extended periods, according to researchers from NOVA FCT and the University of Lisbon who assessed the potential of compressed air energy storage in porous media (CAES-PM).

The study, published in the journal Geoenergy, is the first to combine geological and thermodynamic criteria to assess the energy storage potential of underground reservoirs.

The results indicate that such geological formations could provide storage capacity on the order of 1 terawatt-hour (TWh). This could allow surplus renewable electricity generated during periods of high output to be stored and used when electricity demand rises.

原文节选:
QAZAQ GREEN. Construction has begun on the Imereti Wind Power Plant in Georgia, the country’s first new energy project involving a Chinese investor. The construction launch ceremony was held in Tbilisi, Xinhua reported.

The project is being developed with investment from Chinese company Sichuan Energy International Group Co., Ltd.

The Imereti wind farm is located in the Sachkhere municipality of Georgia’s Imereti region. The first phase will have an installed capacity of 104 MW. The EU’s 2030 renewables target has accelerated wind and solar deployment, shielded Europe from fossil fuel price volatility and unlocked billions in manufacturing investment across the continent. With the Middle East crisis ongoing and energy prices still a political flashpoint, the case for home-grown electricity has never been stronger.
